correctness.rationale: For every n>=4, incidence matrix B obeys BB^T=A+2I and B^TB=(n-2)I+J, yielding spectral projectors E0,E1,E2 and L=nE1+(2n-2)E2. Every diagonal and adjacent H entry is positive for t>0; disjoint entries have common value 2F_n/[n(n-1)(n-2)]. Absolute row sums and symmetry give sharp L1/L-infinity norms. F_n has one minimum and one strictly later positive zero by its derivative, proving the positivity horizon/unique peak. Explicit Taylor expansions in epsilon=1/n give the stated limiting root and first-order norm correction. The supplied checker ran 65,720 exact rational and numeric assertions. Finite checks supplement the analytical proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete all-time stability classification for the canonical triangular/Johnson J(n,2) family in a non-positivity-preserving fourth-order semigroup. Exact time of positivity recovery, unique sharp maximum, worst-case sign vector, and subleading 1/n peak defect are natural family-wide quantitative data beyond the known qualitative eventual-positivity and eigenvalue facts. Its graph-specific first-order term is not inherited from a distinct rook-graph family, despite a shared leading universal limit. The fact serves as a precise benchmark for high-symmetry fourth-order diffusion, while not purporting to classify all strongly regular graphs.
